SystemSketch · Line thickness + contextual menu lab · 2026-09-06

Thickness is its own control now.

Stock tldraw derives a geo shape's stroke width and its label font size from one size rung, so the Font size list was quietly the line-thickness control too. There is now a real thickness control — one registered vocabulary, stacked on a shape and beside a connector — and changing the type no longer moves the outline.

Actual browser recording on the review fixture · walk Thin → Thick → Medium → Thick on the titled rectangle, pick Extra large and watch the outline hold at 7px while the label goes 22px → 32px, then the same three rungs beside the connector's line styles. The ladder, and why these three numbers

Thin · 2px
Medium · 3.5px
Thick · 7px
RungScene unitsAnchored to
Thin2 pxtldraw's own s width
Medium3.5 pxwhat every shape is already drawn at — nothing on an existing board moves
Thick7 pxdouble medium, so the top rung reads as the top

Medium is deliberately what a rectangle is already drawn at, so the control appearing changes nothing on an existing board and an untouched shape reads truthfully as Medium rather than blank. A shape still sitting on tldraw's l or xl rung reports the number it paints and check-marks nothing — the honest reading, not a rung it is not on.

Three sections in one popover — thickness, line style, palette — which is the layout Zach drew.

The reported bug, photographed fixed

How the coupling is actually broken

Adding a control is not enough on its own — an untouched shape still follows its rung. So the Font size write pins the current painted thickness before it moves size (and before a custom px moves scale). Only shapes with no thickness of their own are touched, so it converges instead of rewriting metadata on every keystroke.

export function pinStrokeWidth(editor: Editor): void {
	const updates = editor.getSelectedShapes()
		.filter((shape) => hasAdjustableStrokeWidth(shape) && readStrokeMeta(shape).width === undefined)
		.flatMap((shape) => {
			const px = strokeWidthPxOf(shape)
			if (px === undefined) return []
			const meta = { ...(shape.meta ?? {}) } as JsonObject
			const existing = meta[SYSTEMSKETCH_STROKE_META_KEY]
			meta[SYSTEMSKETCH_STROKE_META_KEY] = {
				...(isRecord(existing) ? (existing as JsonObject) : {}),
				width: p…

Where it is painted

Thickness lives in shape meta, not a StyleProp — a StyleProp only reaches shapes whose util declares it, and geo is tldraw's own shape, so adding one would change a stock record's on-disk schema. The paint rides tldraw's published getCustomDisplayValues seam, which four utils name identically. A Block cable is deliberately excluded: its width is semantic, so the row reads nothing there and is dropped rather than lying.

  • the shape Stroke popover stacks thickness over line style over the palette
  • each thickness rung repaints the rectangle at its own width
  • changing the font size grows the label and leaves the outline alone
  • a chosen thickness carries to the next shape drawn
  • a connector gets the same thickness control beside its line styles, labels off
  • Settings > Menu lab renders the real board, on the app's own editor

  • switching preset recomposes the same registry into the connector surface

  • the physical journey produced zero local console errors

The composition lab · Settings › Menu lab, or ?menu-lab

Zach: “make a generic contextual menu with all the different configuration levers that I can just press myself… add this, hide the labels, stack the thing.” The lab is a lever board wired to the real registry, binder and renderer — not a second menu implementation. If a composition works there it works in the product, and if it is buggy there the product bug reproduces without a canvas selection.

Levers

  • include — whether a registered control is a candidate at all.
  • layout — swatches · row · chips · list · library. row is the “hide the labels” lever.
  • trigger — value · icon · text · toggle · action: what the pill shows.
  • stack — none · above · beside: fold this control into the next included one. above is the shape's stacked popover, beside is the connector's one-line row.
  • value — shared or mixed, so the disagreeing-selection faces are pressable without setting up a selection.
  • new group and ↑ ↓ — the hairline separators and the order, i.e. the recipe itself, printed live as a source literal.

A control stacked onto nothing is named in the readout rather than silently vanishing — quietly disappearing behaviour is exactly what the lab exists to stop.

Prior art it follows (not reinvented)

  • VS Code's menus contribution point. A command is declared once; a surface asks for it with group@order and a when clause. That is the registry / recipe / composeContextualControls split already in this repo.
  • Blender's layout.prop(). Panels are rows and columns that bind to properties; the widget comes from the property's type, never restated at the call site — the registry's glyph and layout fields.
  • Tweakpane / leva / dat.GUI. A control panel generated from a schema of levers: the shape of the lab itself.
  • Zach's own C - Semantic Type Registry — “resolve semantics once, then project them many times”, and “give plugins a constrained contribution point rather than an unbounded new visual language”.
